title: Exact symbolic recurrent-set soundness
statement: Every certificate accepted by v1 or v2 for a trusted supported map supplies a nonempty forward-invariant set of integers at least two.
assumptions: Exact unbounded arithmetic; finite valid expression syntax; exhaustive residue rows; natural affine updates.
map_clock: C3 and C5 use shortcut time; H_sq uses squaring on x_j=2^(2^j), otherwise 1.
proof_summary: Normalization preserves evaluation; positivity proves avoidance; Euclidean residue coverage and exact successor identities close the union. Branch identities also prove parity.
attribution: User-supplied Pass03–Pass05 Collatz corpus; independently reconstructed in h_obstruction_audit.md.
novelty: No historical novelty established; theorem/artifact candidate within corpus.
limitations: No completeness for arbitrary C3 divergence.
significance: Core soundness theorem supporting a finite refutation language.

title: Complete H coverage and all-base separation
statement: H_sq has all bad seeds X={2^(2^j)}; one accepted chart covers X; no infinite subset of X is automatic in any integer base.
assumptions: Canonical finite-base representations; all bases b≥2 considered separately.
map_clock: H_sq is not the compiler H or guarded halving H.
proof_summary: Bad traps are tails; length gaps floor(2^j log_b2)+1 diverge; pumping an infinite regular language would give an impossible arithmetic progression of lengths.
attribution: User-supplied Pass03–Pass05 Collatz corpus; independently reconstructed in h_obstruction_audit.md.
novelty: No historical novelty established; theorem/artifact candidate within corpus.
limitations: Separation across comparison dynamics, not extra proved C3 coverage; H is not run through the C3 automatic checker.

title: v2 sound extension preserving all v1 acceptance
statement: Exact prime-base normalization and quadratic lower bounds preserve all old mathematical certificate acceptance and soundness.
assumptions: Same outer schema and trusted systems; exact trial division and arithmetic.
proof_summary: Old forms have a fixed homomorphic prime-base interpretation; old nonnegative monomials remain so; a quadratic natural-domain minimum plus monotone-remainder value at zero is a valid bound.
attribution: User-supplied Pass03–Pass05 Collatz corpus; independently reconstructed in h_obstruction_audit.md.
novelty: No historical novelty established; theorem/artifact candidate within corpus.
limitations: May cost more resources; accepted base-four H syntax adds encodings, not a proved new semantically detectable C3 case.
significance: Audited conservative enhancement to certificate automation.

title: v2 remains a sufficient, incomplete positivity checker
statement: k^4−2k^3+k^2+2 is everywhere at least two but v2 declines it.
map_clock: Chart parameter k∈N; no dynamical conclusion.
proof_summary: Identity with k²(k−1)²+2 proves positivity; negative cubic coefficient makes the code reject.
attribution: User-supplied Pass03–Pass05 Collatz corpus; independently reconstructed in h_obstruction_audit.md.
novelty: No historical novelty established; theorem/artifact candidate within corpus.
limitations: Does not rule out alternate presentation of its range; no assertion that a Collatz trap is missed.

title: Correct v2 monotonicity is eventual
statement: Every nonconstant eligible v1 chart is strictly increasing from k≥1; v2 charts are eventually strictly increasing and unbounded.
assumptions: Eligibility uses the specified positivity kernels.
map_clock: Natural chart parameter, not orbit time.
proof_summary: Recursive nonempty monomials increase; the v2 quadratic eventually increases unless linear/constant, when positive nonconstant remainder handles the case. k²−6k+11 disproves from-k=1 monotonicity for v2.
attribution: User-supplied Pass03–Pass05 Collatz corpus; independently reconstructed in h_obstruction_audit.md.
novelty: No historical novelty established; theorem/artifact candidate within corpus.
significance: Closes the quantifier/version issue needed in the obstruction proofs.

title: Variable-height semantic obstruction
statement: No finite union of eligible v1/v2 chart images is a G_tow bad trap; fixed-depth expressions with affine updates cannot track its divergent orbits even after positivity relaxation.
assumptions: Finite fixed-depth grammar and residue/affine parameter updates.
map_clock: G_tow: t0=2,t(j+1)=2^t(j); G(n)=2^n on this set, else 1. Distinct from H_sq.
proof_summary: Structural induction bounds each expression by a fixed-height E_h(c(k+2)); increasing chart values in T force variable-height lower bounds. Separately affine updates bound parameters exponentially in time.
attribution: User-supplied Pass03–Pass05 Collatz corpus; independently reconstructed in h_obstruction_audit.md.
novelty: No historical novelty established; theorem/artifact candidate within corpus.
limitations: C3 grows at most exponentially in time, so this growth obstruction cannot transfer to C3.
significance: Genuine semantic limitation, not merely unknown-system-tag rejection.

title: Density-one joint diagonal countercontrol
statement: For the specified eligible charts plus all infinite all-base automatic sets there is a computable map whose density-one bad set has step increments one or two, but no bad trap in either family.
assumptions: Effective enumeration of infinite candidates with uniform search for elements above any threshold; established for both chart versions and all-base automata.
map_clock: F_L next-member map on S, with F(n)=1 off S; depends on chosen language list.
proof_summary: Choose r_e in candidate L_e above previous hole+2 and 2^e; their complement is decidable of density one with gaps≤2; every candidate hits a hole, and finite sets fail invariance under strict increase.
attribution: User-supplied Pass03–Pass05 Collatz corpus; independently reconstructed in h_obstruction_audit.md.
novelty: No historical novelty established; theorem/artifact candidate within corpus.
limitations: Revised interleaved map, not automatically original chart-only F; no theorem about C3; not all conceivable proof languages.
significance: Strongest standalone relative-incompleteness theorem candidate in this portion of corpus.

title: Exact affine H schema and native verifier
statement: The natural affine H schema is valid exactly when a=g=c=d=1 and b=h; a 13-state reusable binary verifier checks its paired-unary framed inputs.
assumptions: Chart P(k)=2^(2^(ak+b)), witness gk+h, successor parameter ck+d; all fields natural.
proof_summary: Injectivity gives a=g,b=h and ac=a,ad=1; natural solutions force unit slopes/update. Accepted prefix is 010101010(11)*00.
attribution: User-supplied Pass03–Pass05 Collatz corpus; independently reconstructed in h_obstruction_audit.md.
novelty: No historical novelty established; theorem/artifact candidate within corpus.
limitations: Specialized solved schema, not arbitrary-expression kernel; framed-prefix parser ignores debris after terminator.

title: 20-state blank-tape H execution reproduced
statement: The full preferred H machine has 20 working states, two symbols, separate halt state, and halts from blank tape in 18 transitions; full-cell-writer reference has 25 states and takes 23.
assumptions: Two-way infinite zero tape; unit L/R moves; initializer included.
map_clock: Known H certificate initialized, not an unknown-counterexample search.
proof_summary: Seven sparse-writer transitions followed by eleven verifier transitions; native tables parsed and independently simulated, snapshot equality verified.

title: Global completeness is weaker than seedwise completeness
statement: For a global blank-tape refuter the missing implication is: if any C3 counterexample exists, some accepted C3 certificate exists. Seedwise recognition requires checked entry into a trap from each bad seed.
proof_summary: Existential global acceptance versus per-seed universal entry obligations; cycles already covered, divergent-orbit coverage remains unresolved.

limitations: Neither completeness theorem is proved by H, G, diagonal F, or the 20-state H execution.
